previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, multiple sclerosis, ulcerative colitis, and asthma was admitted for her fourth cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the infusion well, with no acute complications. Transaminitis recurred and was managed with increased leucovorin. A repeat lumbar puncture was performed due to a lost sample from a prior admission; results are pending. Her chronic right foot pain persisted without a clear cause, and gabapentin was increased to 400 mg three times daily. Oxycodone was also increased for better pain control, and dexamethasone was tapered. She remained stable throughout the admission, with no signs of infection or neurological decline, and was discharged home with outpatient follow-up for lab monitoring and pending CSF results.

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ woman with CNS lymphoma on induction
chemotherapy.  Please assess for interval change.

COMPARISON:  MRI of the head dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1, axial T1, T2 star, FLAIR, T2, and diffusion-weighted
images were acquired.  Following the administration of 6 mL Gadovist, axial T1
and sagittal MP-RAGE as well as coronal and axial reformatted images were
acquired.

FINDINGS:  The previously seen hypointense T1 right frontal mass with
hyperintense rim has decreased in size from the prior examination, now
measuring 2.4 cm AP x 1.0 cm TV x 3.1 cm SI.  Susceptibility artifact is noted
within the lesion, likely reflecting prior blood products.  The surrounding
perilesional edema has also decreased compared to the prior examination. 
There is markedly reduced mass effect on the frontal horn of the right lateral
ventricle.  Small amount of increased FLAIR signal is again noted anterior to
the frontal horn of the left lateral ventricle.  The rim of surrounding
enhancement has also decreased from the prior examination, with only a faint
rim of contrast enhancement persisting, as well as faint enhancement inferior
and medial to the main lesion in the region of the lentiform nucleus, less
prominent than on the prior.  There are no new areas of abnormal enhancement. 
There is no slow diffusion to indicate an acute infarct.

Normal flow voids are preserved in the major intracranial vessels.  There is
global prominence of the ventricles, sulci and subarachnoid spaces, likely
reflecting volume loss.  There is mildly increased prominence of the frontal
horn of the right lateral ventricle, which may reflect ex vacuo dilatation
from the adjacent mass post-treatment.  

Elsewhere, there is a single focus of FLAIR signal hyperintensity in the right
cerebellar hemisphere which is unchanged from prior examinations,
corresponding to prior enhancing lesion, likely residual post treatment
change.  There are no other areas of abnormal signal.  There is a mucus
retention cyst in the right maxillary sinus and minimal mucosal thickening in
the right-sided ethmoid air cells.  The visualized paranasal sinuses,
mastoids, and orbits are otherwise unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Interval marked decrease in size and FLAIR signal abnormality related to right
frontal lobe lesion compatible with the known CNS lymphoma. Stable right
cerebellar FLAIR signal abnormality with decreased ehnhancement. No new
lesion.
